completion_definition: Completed means an initial curated cross-reference pass: the complete supplied English source unit and each retained target passage were read, and each pair has a specific explanation. It does not mean exhaustive coverage or independent specialist approval.
source_language_scope: Supplied English passage comparison; no new Greek, Hebrew, critical-apparatus or UBS6/ECM verification.

deferred_source_units.reason: The invitation places Jesus and His disciples at the Cana wedding. Neighboring family presence and wine shortage do not identify unnamed hosts, and wedding parables are different literary settings.

The each-to-his-house notice remains inside the double-bracketed passage. Jesus' subsequent Mount-of-Olives destination does not establish every person's itinerary or an independently matching departure.
Pilate's ensuing response points to Jesus' own nation and chief priests but does not expressly resolve the question's own-assertion/report alternative. No motive or unspoken answer is supplied.

method: Complete supplied English source units and retained actual target/context passages were read, then independently compared by a second AI-assisted reader. resolved_source_deferrals.previous_reason: The delegation's repeated identity question and need to report to its senders were read with John's answer. Generic envoy or identity inquiries do not provide a sufficiently concrete separate connection to this particular request, and no senders' private motives are invented.

The notice that the envoys were from the Pharisees was read within the baptism-authority inquiry. Broader Pharisee responses in other scenes do not establish the identities, motives or baptismal history of these particular envoys; no group-level conclusion is assigned to them.

The next-day transition with John standing beside two disciples was read with their hearing and following in 1:36–40. The later participant clarification is linked for the explicit hearing-and-following action in 1:37; the distinctive day and standing scene here receive no additional unsupported counterpart.

The feast-master's statement about serving good wine first and the unusually retained good wine was read. Other wine or feast passages do not establish this specific observation and sequence; an unstated historical custom or eschatological identification is not added.

The short Capernaum stay with mother, brothers and disciples was read. Other arrivals or residence notices in Capernaum share the destination but do not establish this family-and-disciples journey or its short duration, so no particular counterpart is retained.

The forty-six-year temple-building reply was read with the ensuing explanation of Jesus' body. Other temple construction dates do not independently establish this figure or the same project, and no external chronology or fabricated harmonization is supplied.

Nicodemus's further question about how these things can happen was read after the water-and-Spirit and wind teaching. A generic repeated expression of difficulty adds little beyond the same conversation, and no separate question is treated as an independent counterpart.

John's baptizing at Aenon near Salim, with much water and people coming, was read. Other baptizing locations do not establish these named sites or their equivalence; no modern identification or unstated ritual procedure is derived from the water notice.
The particular required route through Samaria has no retained precise counterpart; other Samaria journeys have different directions and circumstances.
Jacob's spring, travel weariness and the sixth-hour seating notice remain particular; no unverified well identity or generic fatigue link is credited.
This disciples' food-buying errand is a particular transition; other buying discussions do not establish the errand.
The woman's no-husband reply and Jesus' approval remain specific to her circumstances; they are not equated with another woman's story.
The five past husbands and present non-husband are not independently identified; no allegorical identities or biography is manufactured.
The disciples' wonder and two unspoken questions remain particular; unrelated surprise at Jesus' conversation is not credited.
Leaving this water jar and going to the city remains a particular action; no symbolism for the jar or equivalent abandoned-possession claim is supplied.
The city residents' movement toward Jesus is a brief transition without a retained precise counterpart.
The disciples' request that Rabbi eat remains a particular meal-conversation prompt; unrelated eating scenes are not treated as the same action.
The question about someone bringing food remains this dialogue's specific misunderstanding; a generic food request does not reproduce it.
The crowd's particular observation about the single boat and the disciples' departure has no sufficiently close retained counterpart; no inference about Jesus' exact boarding action is added.
The crowd's boat journey to Capernaum and search transition is unique in these details; no different Gospel crowd journey is treated as the same episode.
The crowd's question about when Jesus arrived has no sufficiently close independent or useful internal counterpart; an unstated travel explanation is not supplied.
Jesus' particular question whether the Twelve also wish to depart is retained without forcing a different disciple question or predicting each individual's response.
The brothers' private directive to leave for Judea so disciples may see His works has no close retained counterpart in its particular actors and purpose.
The hearers' specific speculation about the Greek Dispersion is kept as their question; no actual Greek journey or teaching mission by Jesus is inferred.
The opponents' Galilee-prophet taunt is not endorsed as geographical or prophetic fact, and no unsupported identification of an earlier prophet's home is used to answer it.
The accusers' particular address and repeated caught-in-the-act charge has no additional sufficiently useful counterpart beyond the legal-background comparisons attached to the surrounding units.
The one-by-one departure beginning with the elders and the remaining woman is distinctive. A motive such as a supplied conscience clause is not inserted into this edition's text.
The identity question and the exact reply 'Why do I even speak to you at all?' are preserved. A familiar alternative rendering about speaking from the beginning is not imported.
The neighbors' identity dispute and the man's 'I am he' are retained without equating his ordinary identification with Jesus' distinct identity sayings.
The man's lack of knowledge of Jesus' current whereabouts is a particular narrative detail; no broader ignorance of Jesus or different missing-person scene is inferred.
The parents' combined interview question about sonship, congenital blindness, and present sight has no close retained counterpart as a whole; unrelated family hearings are not identified with it.
The parents' stated limits of knowledge and referral to their adult son are retained without deciding an unstated degree of knowledge or pairing a generic ignorance statement.

The two-day stay after hearing of Lazarus's illness was read. Other delays or absence statements do not independently reproduce this exact stay, and no unstated motive or travel-time calculation is supplied.

Bethany's approximately fifteen-stadia distance from Jerusalem was read. Other Olivet, Bethany or Sabbath-journey notices do not independently establish this particular distance or a precise site identity.
Jesus' still being outside the village at Martha's meeting place was read. General meeting and travel notices do not independently establish this position at this point in the sequence.
The where-have-you-laid-him question and come-and-see reply were read. Other invitations to see Jesus concern different objects and purposes and do not establish this tomb-location exchange.

The council's fear of Roman action against place and nation if all believe was read. Other political fears do not establish these speakers' particular prediction, and the prediction is not treated as independently verified history.
The specific Philip-to-Andrew-to-Jesus message relay was read. Other introductions to Jesus do not independently reproduce these intermediaries, their order or the message.
The crowd's thunder-versus-angel interpretations of the heavenly sound were read. Other heavenly voices do not reproduce these particular interpretations or participants.
Peter's request for hands and head as well as feet was read. General washings or priestly-body regulations do not independently reproduce his request or settle its full meaning.

The other disciple's acquaintance with the high priest, conversation with the woman doorkeeper and bringing Peter inside were read in their full order. Other courtyard accounts do not reproduce this particular admission through an unnamed intermediary, and that disciple is not automatically identified as the beloved disciple or given a personal name.

The instruction to bring some newly caught fish was read with the existing fire, fish and bread and Peter's subsequent hauling. Other food requests and the earlier crowd-feeding scenes do not supply this particular catch-to-breakfast instruction, and no generic serving or command-response link is added.

Peter's question about the other disciple was read with Jesus' conditional answer and the rumor correction. Those explain the same exchange rather than supplying a separate counterpart; generic curiosity or judgment passages do not establish Peter's motive or the other disciple's future.

First Kings17:10–13 was freshly read: Elijah requests water in a vessel and bread from a widow. Unlike this draw-and-bring-to-the-feast-master command, it addresses him as recipient and then a different food provision. The broad request/service resemblance remains insufficiently particular for retention.

The husband-fetching instruction was reread with the no-husband reply. No husband is narrated as fetched, and generic spouse-summoning passages would not supply this request or its unexplained full purpose.

The question was reread with the actual woman's reply and Jesus' instruction. They complete this exchange, but no different absolution scene is made the same event or a further comparison for these departed accusers.

The stated for-this-reason referral was reread with9:21–22. Its immediate causal and repeated wording is already considered in the particular9:21 comparison; no additional cross-passage relation is assigned merely to repeat that comment.

The request to identify the Son of Man was reread with the exact following self-identification. That title is not changed to Son of God, and no unrelated who question is made the same particular request to believe.

Pilate's increased fear is explicitly linked to the preceding allegation. Other warnings or judicial anxieties do not establish that cause or justify an unstated inner belief, and the wife's different experience is not transferred to him.

The refusal to revise the placard was reread with the requested change. A rule about irrevocable royal decrees would not establish Pilate's legal obligation or particular motive here; no general law is imposed on this rhetorical reply.
Jesus remains in Galilee after the actual not-going statement, before the later private journey. No yet is inserted into7:8 or unreported duration used to harmonize the sequence.
